title: During an Eclipse, the Moon's Shadow Moves Over 1,000 mph

scenes.text: During an eclipse, the Moon's shadow moves over 1,000 miles an hour.
That's the dark shadow sweeping across the ground toward you.
NASA said the 2024 shadow crossed Earth at more than 1,500 miles an hour.
In 2017 it was only about 70 miles wide, and totality lasted at most two minutes forty seconds.
It's so fast you couldn't chase it, even in a supersonic jet.
A shadow you can never outrun.

description:
During a total solar eclipse, the Moon's shadow sweeps over Earth faster than 1,000 miles an hour.
NASA put the 2024 shadow at more than 1,500 miles an hour.
Even a supersonic jet could not keep up with it.
Have you ever seen a total eclipse?
first_comment: Have you ever seen a total eclipse? What did the shadow feel like?
